find: Elastane (brand name Lycra) is a polyurethane-based fibre capable of stretching to five to seven times its original length and recovering fully (some sources cite up to 8×; 5–6× is the most commonly cited figure) and recovering fully.
replace: Elastane (brand name Lycra) is a polyurethane-based fibre that can stretch to about five times its original length and then recover its shape fully.
note: F1: elastane stretches to about five times its length; the sentence also carried an unremoved drafting note and a duplicated clause.

expect: Which synthetic fibre can stretch up to eight times its original length and recover fully?
value: Which synthetic fibre can stretch to about five times its original length and recover fully?
note: F2: 'eight times' is wrong and contradicts the corrected lesson text; the keyed answer (Elastane) is unchanged.

find: Legally required for children's nightwear (UK Night Clothes Safety Regulations), upholstered furniture and contract (public building) soft furnishings.
replace: Legally required for children's nightwear (the Nightwear (Safety) Regulations 1985), upholstered furniture and contract (public building) soft furnishings.
note: F5: the 'UK Night Clothes Safety Regulations' does not exist; the UK instrument is the Nightwear (Safety) Regulations 1985 (SI 1985/2043).

expect: UK Night Clothes Safety Regulations require it to reduce the risk of burn injuries if the fabric comes near a flame.
value: The Nightwear (Safety) Regulations 1985 require it. The finish reduces the risk of serious burns if the garment meets a flame.
note: F6: same invented statute name, in the card the student revises from.

find: This paired structure — one advantage, one limitation per method — is exactly what the mark scheme rewards at 6 and 8 marks.
replace: This paired structure — one advantage, one limitation per method — gives a longer answer the balance it needs.
note: F7: removes an unverifiable claim about what a mark scheme rewards; the advice itself is kept.

find: responsible for approximately 10% of global carbon emissions and 20% of industrial water pollution
replace: responsible for an estimated 2% to 8% of global carbon emissions and about 20% of industrial water pollution
note: F8: the 10% figure is a 2018 press-release number the later studies do not support; 2-8% is the range the UN bodies now quote. The water figure is unchanged.

find: Post-consumer textile recycling rates remain below 1% globally despite growing collection infrastructure.
replace: Less than 1% of clothing worldwide is recycled into new clothing, despite growing collection infrastructure.
note: F9: the under-1% figure is fibre-to-fibre recycling only; overall collection and downcycling is far higher, as the same paragraph says.
